Hooked: How South Africa's towing industry preys on consumers

By: Layton Beard | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How the First Help towing company is preying on consumers ...

Unique Selling Point:
First Help is the biggest towing operator in South Africa but among it's fleet of towing operators there appear to be rogue elements who continually scam and take advantage of consumers, especially in a time of need after an accident.

This story is made more topical because of the time of year and presents insight into how the towing industry preys on motorists.

Summary:
Under-regulated, opportunistic, and often predatory, the towing industry thrives in a grey zone. And with more than eight million uninsured vehicles on the road, many motorists only learn the true cost of being in a crash after the dust has settled. Tow trucks are a familiar sight, skipping lights and ramping curbs to be first on the scene of an accident – but what happens after your vehicle is towed can come as a nasty shock. Exorbitant fees, vanishing vehicles, and costly repairs all add up to skyrocketing anxiety and expense for owners. Carte Blanche exposes the darker side of an industry few understand, and most encounter only in moments of crisis.

Further information:
Not a PSA but will have an element of consumer advice.
Story focusses on the state of the towing industry with specific reference to First Help, the largest towing and recovery operator in South Africa.

Press Release:


Hooked

Under-regulated, opportunistic, and often predatory, the towing industry thrives in a grey zone. And with more than eight million uninsured vehicles on the road, many motorists only learn the true cost of being in a crash after the dust has settled. Tow trucks are a familiar sight, skipping lights and ramping curbs to be first on the scene of an accident – but what happens after your vehicle is towed can come as a nasty shock. Exorbitant fees, vanishing vehicles, and costly repairs all add up to skyrocketing anxiety and expense for owners. Carte Blanche exposes the darker side of an industry few understand, and most encounter only in moments of crisis.

Producer: Layton Beard | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


(Masa) If you’ve ever had the misfortune of being in a car accident, you’ll know you’re frightened, you’re shaken, and you’re overwhelmed and, hopefully, you’re not injured. All you want is to get the logistics out of the way in a fair manner. But what happens when you’re taken advantage of in your vulnerable moment?

(Masa) Johannesburg student Peter-John Farrell was out with his friends on a Friday night in June when he struck an oil slick around a bend and flipped his Suzuki Swift on its roof. His car was a wreck; his emotions were running high and, fortunately, no-one was injured. An operator from a towing company called First Help was soon on the scene …

(Peter-John Farrell) He came to me and asked where I’d like the car to be towed to, I said I live less than a kilometre from where we are now and I’d like the car to be towed to my house then he said ‘cool, perfect, we’ll sort that out for you’ you’ll just have to pay R1200.

(Masa) But John’s car never arrived … following several calls to First Help, a trip to the police station, and stopping to talk to other tow operators on the road, John was advised to visit a storage yard in Sophiatown on Joburg’s West Rand. It’s here where he eventually found his car. But the storage yard refused to release it. Desperate, John reported the matter to the police.

(Peter-John Farrell) … we spoke to the police officer. He says they get cases like this all the time where the First Help have agreed to tow the car to people’s houses and then they just take it into storage and charge ten times what was expected of the person.

(Masa) And that’s exactly what happened to John – he had to pay more than thirteen thousand Rand to release his car. Unfortunately, John’s story isn’t unique…

(Ignatius Delport) They told me nothing, they just said R2800, they will tow it to Probeat …

(Masa) Centurion attorney Ignatius Delport was in an accident in Pretoria in June. He says a First Help tow operator was quickly on the scene and agreed to take his car to an assessment centre. It would only cost him two thousand eight hundred Rand.

(Ignatius Delport) They didn’t show me any specific clauses, they didn’t enlighten me on all the fynskrif (fine print) on the other side of the contract, it was like just: … “Nee oom, ons help vir jou gou, moenie worry nie, moenie worry nie …
(Insider Subtitles) No, don’t worry, don’t worry, we’ll quickly help you

(Masa) Days later, Ignatius received an invoice for fourteen thousand three hundred Rand that included charges for storage fees, fuel and other expenses which he says were never disclosed to him. When he queried the amount, he was told he had signed for all the services…

(Ignatius Delport) Only when I got the quote and I started questioning it, then I looked at the back of the form and I … Oh hell, I signed for this. But it is wrong because they … gave one impression next to the road everything is R2800 and then they come back and don’t disclose anything and come back and say oh, now you owe us R14300 otherwise you can’t get your car.

(Masa) But even those in a minor crash – those who still have presence of mind after an incident – are misled. For Christo Smit it went beyond simple misrepresentation – he was actively hoodwinked by First Help. In August, his VW Polo was lightly struck by a truck in eastern Joburg. Both he and the truck driver pulled over to examine the damage, while a nearby metro police officer also stopped. Christo says he noticed a First Help tow operator hovering at the scene as well, taking photographs while he was speaking to the police. Christo declined to be towed but minutes later, as he was driving to a meeting, he received a call from someone claiming to be his insurer. The caller had all of Christo’s details, including his ID number and car’s VIN number…

(Christo Smit) I don’t know anybody else really, even close friends or family, that’s got that information available, on hand. I pulled off my car’s discs, licence discs, and I confirmed that the VIN number is exactly what the guy just read out to me on the phone. Based on that information received from them, I believed that it is the insurance company that I’m talking to.

(Masa) The caller told Christo his Tracker system had alerted them to the accident. He was instructed not to drive any further. Christo pulled over and, moments later, handed his car to the tow operator – First Help … He later discovered the caller was NOT from his insurer and he now faced a thirteen thousand Rand bill to get his car back.

(Masa) R13 0000 for this invoice, for a service that you didn’t want?
(Christo Smit) Exactly, you’re being scammed into an amount of R13 0000 to release your car for some service that you did not ask them basically to render to you.
(Masa) And you had to pay that?
(Christo Smit) There’s no option.

(Masa) Towing associations say there are only a few rotten apples in the industry.

(Masa) SATRA – the South African Towing and Recovery Association – is a voluntary association comprising big and small contractors as members – including First Help. Association Chairperson André van der Merwe says they prefer to deal with complaints through mediation.

(André van der Merwe) We don’t take measures against our members we rather have our members cooperating with us in redressing wherever they do commit these wrongs. So, the consumer comes to me, comes to SATRA, says I have a complaint, invariably they’ll phone in – if it’s a SATRA member I am in a position to intervene because I have locus standi – if it’s not a SATRA member I can’t intervene. You must remember that SATRA by no means represents the entire towing industry…

(Masa) André points to a lack of enforcement for problems in the towing industry. He says self-regulation is difficult …

(André van der Merwe) The towing industry is a microcosm of broader society; the prisons are full of people who don’t adhere to things; so, we’re no different in context than the rest of society in South Africa, there’s different elements and components. There are those who will abide every time, there are those who will do it some of the time, and there are those who just simply rogues … the rogues … it’s a problem.

(Masa) So, is First Help one of these rogue operators? Looking at online reviews and social media posts, it’s difficult to ignore this pattern of alleged misrepresentation…

(Masa) We reached out to First Help and offered them a sit-down interview. They didn’t want to talk to us, instead referring us to André. But he didn’t want to get into specifics, preferring to speak about problems in the industry in general…

(André van der Merwe) Now I did ask you let’s not be mentioning names … and you’re mentioning names …
(Masa) … because they’ve been mentioned by the case studies …
(André van der Merwe) No, no, listen … no, but hang on, let’s also respect each other in this interview …
(Masa) … let’s also let each finish each other’s … can I finish a sentence …
(André van der Merwe) Let’s also respect each other …
(Masa) 100%

(André van der Merwe) We set from the outset it’s a generalised … and we not going to point specifics …
(Masa) André …
(André van der Merwe) If you want to get me to help, it you want to get me to help I will help and we do help and you mustn’t labour under the misconception that we are toothless …

(Masa) In a later written response, First Help said the issues pointed out to them are not unique to First Help and are a national, industry-wide problem. They say education and digital innovation are required to solve the problem. They also added they would be launching a new initiative in early 2026 to provide uninsured motorists clarity and transparency.

(Masa) So, you’ve been involved in a car accident – whether insured or uninsured – what should you do, who should you call … and who can you trust?

(Wendy Knowler) Before the accident – what you must do right now – is if you are uninsured, find a number of a towing association of your liking or both and put that in your phone – 24-hour service – so at least you’re not completely alone, you’ve got someone to give you a bit of advice or say this company or that company or whatever, so you’re not completely on your own.

(Masa) Cape Town-based Consumer Journalist Wendy Knowler has covered issues in the towing industry for many years. She says being in control at the scene of an accident is critical to ensure you protect your rights …

(Wendy Knowler) If you are insured, put your insurer’s emergency number in your phone, under their name, so that when the bad thing happens and you need to make that call, you must make that call yourself, don’t let anyone else make the call for you, you know, it’s one less thing for you to worry about, it’s there at your fingertips, and you make that call so you’re in control.

(Masa) The National Consumer Commission or NCC says it handles complaints as they come in and says a blanket approach to problems in the towing industry is inappropriate. It says it has only received five complaints about the towing industry the past two years and encourages those who experienced problems with towers to lodge complaints. But, until there is proper enforcement and better regulation of the industry, it appears that motorists remain on their own at the moment they need it most.

He says self-regulation is difficult … (André van der Merwe) The towing industry is a microcosm of broader society; the prisons are full of people who don’t adhere to things; so, we’re no different in context than the rest of society in South Africa, there’s different elements and components. There are those who will abide every time, there are those who will do it some of the time, and there are those who just simply rogues … the rogues … it’s a problem. (Masa) So, is First Help one of these rogue operators? Looking at online reviews and social media posts, it’s difficult to ignore this pattern of alleged misrepresentation… (Masa) We reached out to First Help and offered them a sit-down interview. They didn’t want to talk to us, instead referring us to André. But he didn’t want to get into specifics, preferring to speak about problems in the industry in general… (André van der Merwe) Now I did ask you let’s not be mentioning names … and you’re mentioning names … (Masa) … because they’ve been mentioned by the case studies … (André van der Merwe) No, no, listen … no, but hang on, let’s also respect each other in this interview … (Masa) … let’s also let each finish each other’s … can I finish a sentence … (André van der Merwe) Let’s also respect each other … (Masa) 100% (André van der Merwe) We set from the outset it’s a generalised … and we not going to point specifics … (Masa) André … (André van der Merwe) If you want to get me to help, it you want to get me to help I will help and we do help and you mustn’t labour under the misconception that we are toothless … (Masa) In a later written response, First Help said the issues pointed out to them are not unique to First Help and are a national, industry-wide problem. They say education and digital innovation are required to solve the problem. They also added they would be launching a new initiative in early 2026 to provide uninsured motorists clarity and transparency. (Masa) So, you’ve been involved in a car accident – whether insured or uninsured – what should you do, who should you call … and who can you trust? (Wendy Knowler) Before the accident – what you must do right now – is if you are uninsured, find a number of a towing association of your liking or both and put that in your phone – 24-hour service – so at least you’re not completely alone, you’ve got someone to give you a bit of advice or say this company or that company or whatever, so you’re not completely on your own. (Masa) Cape Town-based Consumer Journalist Wendy Knowler has covered issues in the towing industry for many years. She says being in control at the scene of an accident is critical to ensure you protect your rights … (Wendy Knowler) If you are insured, put your insurer’s emergency number in your phone, under their name, so that when the bad thing happens and you need to make that call, you must make that call yourself, don’t let anyone else make the call for you, you know, it’s one less thing for you to worry about, it’s there at your fingertips, and you make that call so you’re in control. (Masa) The National Consumer Commission or NCC says it handles complaints as they come in and says a blanket approach to problems in the towing industry is inappropriate. It says it has only received five complaints about the towing industry the past two years and encourages those who experienced problems with towers to lodge complaints. But, until there is proper enforcement and better regulation of the industry, it appears that motorists remain on their own at the moment they need it most. ENDS

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): How the First Help towing company is preying on consumers ...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: First Help is the biggest towing operator in South Africa but among it's fleet of towing operators there appear to be rogue elements who continually scam and take advantage of consumers, especially in a time of need after an accident. This story is made more topical because of the time of year and presents insight into how the towing industry preys on motorists.
metadata.Summary: Under-regulated, opportunistic, and often predatory, the towing industry thrives in a grey zone. And with more than eight million uninsured vehicles on the road, many motorists only learn the true cost of being in a crash after the dust has settled. Tow trucks are a familiar sight, skipping lights and ramping curbs to be first on the scene of an accident – but what happens after your vehicle is towed can come as a nasty shock. Exorbitant fees, vanishing vehicles, and costly repairs all add up to skyrocketing anxiety and expense for owners. Carte Blanche exposes the darker side of an industry few understand, and most encounter only in moments of crisis.
metadata.Further information: Not a PSA but will have an element of consumer advice. Story focusses on the state of the towing industry with specific reference to First Help, the largest towing and recovery operator in South Africa.
